clue.text: Leaders who may turn out to be real idiots

indicators.note: what may turn out differently is something re-formed, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Politicians at the head of the party who could prove to be complete fools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like people in charge, but newspaper leaders are their opinion columns. 'may turn out to be' rearranges REAL IDIOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading articles, stating its own opinion, are called leaders.

clue.text: Face being confined to bed?

parts.note: not an invalid laid up, but the marked face of a garden sun clock standing in a flower bed

explanation.definitionFit: A clock or sundial face, with its marked hours, is what this word names.

clue.text: Now the aim of boys wanting to take out girls

definitions.text: the aim of boys wanting to take out girls

explanation.surface: What lads hope for when they ask girls out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to the present; read literally it is the purpose of asking someone out.

clue.text: Conducted a bag search

parts.note: ran means managed or conducted
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: Someone went through a bag looking for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through a place thoroughly and roughly, looking for things, is to search it.

clue.text: Egg on a steak, say

parts.note: steak sounds like stake, and a stake is a wager, a bet

explanation.surface: Order an egg on top of the steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' looks like breakfast but means encourage; 'say' signals that steak is heard as stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage or urge someone, often to wrongdoing, is to incite them.

clue.text: Something that's essential when raising fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting, so the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a must is something essential
as means when

explanation.surface: Growing fruit needs one indispensable thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns A MUST AS into SATSUMA, read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a kind of mandarin orange, a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Rambling with company in a natural setting

indicators.note: in a setting means placed inside, so the company abbreviation goes within the word for natural

parts.note: inherent means natural, innate

explanation.surface: Wandering about with friends in a countryside setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' suggests a country walk; it is the definition, meaning disjointed talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that wanders without order or logic is disjointed and unclear.

clue.text: Just sufficient reason for a place of diversion

parts.note: fair means adequate, just good enough
ground means a basis or reason

explanation.surface: A barely adequate justification for somewhere to have fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor site with rides and sideshows is a place of amusement.

clue.text: Either way it was of some worth in India

definitions.text: it was of some worth in India

indicators.note: the word reads the same from left to right or right to left, so it works either way round

parts.words: it was of some worth in India
parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something reads the same in both directions and once had value on the subcontinent.
explanation.walkthrough: The anna was a small coin of British India, worth a sixteenth of a rupee.
explanation.definitionFit: This former coin of British India had a small monetary value, a sixteenth of a rupee.

clue.text: Slug possibly represents danger to stray pets

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off course, so the letters of danger and pets wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A slug, perhaps, is a threat to pets that wander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stray' reworks DANGER and PETS together; 'represents' and 'to' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is one example of a creature that eats a gardener's plants.

clue.text: Fully enjoy the taste

explanation.surface: Make the most of the flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something is to enjoy it fully; as a noun the word also means a distinctive flavour.

clue.text: New dance in church shows rhythm

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: new here means remade, so the letters of dance are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newly devised dance performed in church displays a beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges DANCE to ADENC, which goes 'in' CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is the rise and fall or measured beat of sound, a kind of rhythm.

clue.text: Taxi required in case there's heavy luggage

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
a trunk is a large case

explanation.surface: A cab is needed in case there are heavy bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in case' looks like the stock phrase meaning 'should it happen', but the two words do separate jobs here.
explanation.definitionFit: A large travelling chest sized for a ship's cabin is bulky baggage.

clue.text: Food that may be undishable!

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters of the word could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A food so unpleasant it could not be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges the made-up word UNDISHABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-veined Danish cheese is a foodstuff.

clue.text: Is in good time but nearly loses a point

indicators.note: loses means the word nearly drops a letter

parts.note: N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone is punctual, but almost drops a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead of schedule, before the expected hour, means punctual or soon.

clue.text: He's not paid for taking a friend to the old city

parts.note: a mate is a friend
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Someone unpaid takes a pal along on a trip to an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: UR, the biblical city of the Chaldees, is a crossword favourite for 'old city'.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsalaried participant, one who plays for love rather than money, is a non-professional.

clue.text: A lot to collect

parts.note: a mass is a lot, a large quantity

explanation.surface: There is a great deal to gather.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together a large quantity, such as a fortune, is to accumulate.

clue.text: Sounding more relaxed with one's destiny

indicators.note: sounding tells us that the word for more relaxed is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: calmer means more relaxed

explanation.surface: A calmer-sounding person accepts what fate holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in non-rhotic British speech, where CALMER and KARMA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist thought, karma is the fate that one's deeds bring upon one.

clue.text: Sea-bed

parts.note: not the ocean floor but a bed slept in at sea, on board ship

explanation.definitionFit: A narrow shelf bed on a ship is the usual sleeping berth for sailors.

clue.text: May be ordered off for eating

definitions.text: May be ordered off for eating

parts.words: May be ordered off for eating
parts.note: looks like a player sent off, but it is the card from which diners order food

explanation.definitionFit: The bill of fare in a restaurant lists the dishes a diner chooses from.

clue.text: Cut Sophia Loren's initials on a tree

indicators.note: initials are the first letters of a name, here of the actress's two names

parts.note: the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone carves the film star's monogram into a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initials' takes S and L from Sophia Loren, and ASH, the tree, follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: To gash or slit something with a sweeping stroke is to cut it.

clue.text: It may be used defensively or offensively

definitions.text: It may be used defensively or offensively

parts.words: It may be used defensively or offensively
parts.note: stacked up as a flood or bullet barrier, or swung as a cosh to strike someone

explanation.definitionFit: A sack of grit serves as a barricade, and as a verb means to bludgeon or ambush.

clue.text: Horrible house I'd demolish

indicators.note: demolish means knock down, so the letters of house and I'd are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An ugly house that someone would knock down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely ugly or repulsive is dreadful.

clue.text: Organ brilliant with flowers

parts.note: the nose is the organ of smell
gay in its older sense means bright and brilliant

explanation.surface: A splendid instrument decked out with blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the church instrument but is a body part; GAY is used in its old sense of bright.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bunch of sweet-scented blooms is a posy.

clue.text: Able to see, saw

explanation.surface: Having vision, one spotted something.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with working vision is not blind; as a verb, the word also means caught sight of.

clue.text: Get a move on, having reached double figures

parts.note: has means having, possessing
ten is the first number of two digits

explanation.surface: Hurry up now you are past nine years old.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry or speed up is to move faster.

clue.text: Joke too blue, perhaps

parts.note: to rib someone is to joke with or tease them
too means also, and so and

explanation.surface: A gag that is rather too risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests smutty, but a blue riband is a ribbon awarded as first prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue ribbon is an example of a riband, the old spelling of ribbon.

clue.text: Where to see the Taj Mahal in a gracious setting

definitions.text: Where to see the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: the setting holds a jewel, so the place name sits inside the words a gracious

explanation.surface: The Taj Mahal can be seen amid elegant surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a gracious setting' places the answer inside A GRACIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city on the Yamuna is home to the famous mausoleum.

clue.text: A donkey almost berserk

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey that has nearly gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is British slang for a donkey; 'almost' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild in a frenzy is going out of control.

clue.text: What old lags have for sack sewing?

definitions.text: What old lags have for sack sewing?

parts.words: What old lags have for sack sewing?
parts.note: convicts once stitched mailbags as prison work, and a long sentence leaves plenty of hours to fill

explanation.walkthrough: An 'old lag' is British slang for a habitual convict; sewing mailbags was a traditional prison job.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a great deal of time available, punning on sacks sewn in jail.

clue.text: Anti American intelligence

parts.note: being against something is saying no to it
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Opposition to the United States intelligence service.
explanation.definitionFit: Common sense or practical wit is the meaning of this Greek-derived word.

clue.text: Evergreen creeper

parts.note: looks like an ivy-type plant, but means a reptile that creeps through green growth

explanation.definitionFit: The common European water snake slithers through the lawn and grassland, hence green and creeping.
